items.text: Fixed the male avatar's right leg.
Custom levels with their own speed no longer play out of sync.
Make a level from any song you own. ADD LEVELS now opens a page in your browser that listens to the song and builds a level from it.
Maps from other rhythm games that use mods only to place notes now import. The import page says plainly which files it takes, and a level that cannot be used tells you why.
Your own levels count toward Warm-Up, Face Off and Workout, and toward Mighty Five and On Repeat when the song runs longer than a minute. S ranks and leaderboards stay with the built-in songs.
CUSTOM LEVELS now comes first in the song list.
Hold an arrow key, the d-pad or a stick to keep scrolling, or hold your hand out to the side.
Menu gestures respond more reliably, and the phone no longer presses cards by itself right after it connects. The setting is now called MENU GESTURES and sits in SYSTEM.
Escape on the main menu asks whether you want to quit.
SHOW CAMERA EDGES marks on the track where the camera's view ends, so you know before you step out of it.
IN-GAME PREVIEW sets the corner view to Off, Normal or Large, and with SHOW HUD off nothing is drawn over the game, for streaming.
REDUCED FLASH in GRAPHICS steadies the lasers and the floor and softens hit effects.
LIGHT FRAME puts a light border around the screen, so the TV lights you up for the camera in a dark room.
Your first song names each move as it comes: slash blocks, catch rings, kick balls, stomp, slide and dodge.
Steam Game Recording marks every song you play with its difficulty, rank and score, so a run is easy to find and clip later.
A hit ball no longer bounces back at you off the tunnel wall.
Phone tracking recovers by itself when the system drops the connection.
The game opens behind a loading screen instead of a stalled first menu.
Confirming with a gamepad keeps working after the menu has been steered by movement.

items.text: SSS is in. A new top rank sits above SS, and every line under it moved down, so runs that used to flatten out at S finally show what they were worth. Nothing you already earned moves backwards: every saved result keeps its letter or gets a better one, and the same run scores more than it used to. Your old bests are sitting there, beatable. Go take them.

Songs start when you are ready. A level opens on a loading screen instead of a frozen first beat, and the count-in is five seconds instead of ten, so the wait is you getting into position rather than you watching nothing.
A gesture you half caught keeps your streak. A line of rings counts as one thing and a slide stops breaking in the middle, so the combo you feel is the combo you get.
Sound lines up. AUDIO OFFSET in settings dials out the delay your TV or speakers add, and "+" on TIMING OFFSET means later again, exactly the way it reads.
Tracking holds steadier. A phone lying on its side moves you as far as one standing up, a phone that reboots is found again without restarting the game, and ankles no longer flip around the shin.
New camera work. VIEW FOLLOW rides the body instead of watching from a fixed seat, marked PREVIEW while it settles.

The menus got a proper pass. Settings are grouped into GAMEPLAY, BODY TRACKING, GRAPHICS, AUDIO, PLAYER 2 and SYSTEM, the results page and the leaderboards are redrawn, cards carry a rank badge and a difficulty chip, and text stays inside its frame.
Tutorial clips play on Steam Deck and on Linux. Where Proton could not decode the video they run as frames now, instead of a placeholder telling you it cannot play.
New Video Tutorial Added
A new tutorial covering stomps and slides has been added.
It will automatically play once before the level selector on your first launch after the update.
Improved Motion Control Navigation
Menu navigation using motion controls is now smoother and more responsive for a better overall experience.
macOS Fix
Resolved an issue where tutorial videos were not playing properly on macOS.
